title: imf say global growth track reach 3 2026 risks remain high 2026 09 10
text:
WASHINGTON, Sept 10 (Reuters) - The IMF on Thursday said the global ​economy had weathered the ‌energy shock caused by the war in the Middle East ​better than feared and ​global economic output was still ⁠expected to expand by about ​3% in 2026, but ​it cautioned that risks remained high.
Julie Kozack, spokesperson for the International Monetary ​Fund, said oil and ​gas prices remained high and the ‌energy ⁠shock from the war was not over. Global debt pressures were also mounting and ​the ​disinflation ⁠process over the 2022 cost of living crisis ​had stalled, she ​told ⁠reporters.
Kozack told a regular IMF briefing that global inflation expectations ⁠had ​risen but ​remain well-anchored over the longer run.
